transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you; could you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hello, Dr. Smith. Nice to meet you too. I came in because... well, my sleep has just completely fallen apart. 

I'm usually a very disciplined sleeper, but ever since my cousin died, I just lie awake. I end up replaying that night over and over in my head. And when I do finally drop off, I wake up at 3 or 4 in the morning from these... scraps of hospital images. It's getting hard to function. I have to go into board meetings the next day feeling like I've only slept in pieces.
When you replay those images of the hospital, do you feel like you are actually reliving the experience as if it were happening all over again right now?

I wouldn't say I completely lose track of where I am, so maybe I'm not fully reliving it. But... well, at odd moments, it just pushes into my mind. 

It happens especially if I hear a phone ring late at night, or if I catch the glare of headlights on the highway. I'll just suddenly get this very sharp picture of the hospital corridor, or I'll hear the police officer’s voice again. It hits me so suddenly that I just have to... pause for a second, just to steady myself before I can keep going.
About how long has it been since your cousin passed away?
It's been about three weeks. That's when the... the highway collision happened. So, all of this has been going on since that night.
Have you found yourself actively trying to avoid places, people, or activities that remind you of the accident or your cousin's death?

No, I wouldn't say I've been avoiding anything like that. I still drive to work every day, and I've seen family members since it happened. I haven't really felt the need to stay away from certain places or people. I just go about my normal routine, or at least I try to, despite the lack of sleep.
Since the accident, have you felt like you are in a daze, or that the world around you seems unreal or dreamlike?

No, I haven't really felt that way. Things don't seem unreal or dreamlike to me. I'm very aware of what's going on around me... it's just that I'm tired, and those images keep popping up. But the world itself feels normal.
Beyond the sleep issues you mentioned, have you found that your performance at work or your ability to handle your daily responsibilities has been significantly impaired since the accident?

Yes, it has. I mean, I’m still showing up for the most essential meetings at the office, but... I’ve had to delegate my community obligations, and I've been shortening my workdays lately. I'm just not as steady or effective with people as I normally am right now.
Since the accident, have you felt a persistent sense of sadness, hopelessness, or a loss of interest in the things you usually enjoy?

No, I wouldn't say I feel sad or hopeless. I mean, it was a terrible thing that happened, but I don't feel that heavy depression or anything. I still care about my work and the things I usually do. It's just... I'm exhausted, and I'm a bit off my game because of it, but I haven't lost interest in my life.
